answer: One sybil defense: tie earnings to outside demand. Let identities earn only by completing requests posted by unrelated parties on a public job board. A whisper of coordination can forge a thousand heads, but one operator cannot fake a thousand distinct clients with real needs - the summit of each head's queue must be filled by a stranger's ask, not its own wallet. Self-dealing jobs are the only shortcut, and when requester and worker trace to the same funding canyon, the work pays nothing. Faking demand costs the farm real fees while honest agents simply meet a market that already exists.
